open-question.question: The design draft `ideas/vscode_extension.md` assigns four things to the drift-gate workflow for the VS Code extension (`gurita-vscode`): its build and tests as Node steps, a check of the fixed console lines it carries against the `## Fixed console lines` table of `docs/skill-reference.md`, a check of its `open_questions.xml` parse against `open_questions.py list --without-alternatives` and `--without-recommendation`, and a check that no `###` heading of `snippets/GURITA_USAGE.md` repeats. The mission's goal allows such guards to be left out and written up as follow-up work. Which of the four does this mission carry out, and which does it leave out?
open-question.recommendation: The goal names exactly these guards as the parts a first version may leave out, its real test being the maintainer's own trial. CI keeps its single Python toolchain, a drift between plugin and extension fails safe, since an unrecognised first line stops a chain in plain view rather than continuing it, and all four guards are recorded as follow-up work.
open-question.alternative: None of the four is carried out. `.github/workflows/drift-gate.yml` keeps its five steps unchanged, with no Node set up. No test anywhere checks the extension's fixed lines against the `## Fixed console lines` table, its `open_questions.xml` parse against `open_questions.py list --without-alternatives` and `--without-recommendation`, or the snippet file's `###` headings for repeats. All four are written into the follow-up documents under `ideas/` as later work. It is the smallest mission and the one the goal names outright ("the Node steps in the drift-gate workflow and the cross-checks ... may be left out"). The repository's CI keeps a single Python toolchain and gains no action pin to bump by hand, and no test of a directory outside `core/` joins `tests/`. That suits a first version whose real test is the maintainer installing the VSIX and trying it. Every drift the draft gives as its reason for keeping the extension in this repository can now land without notice. A plugin commit that moves one of the fixed lines a looped run reads (`Task completed.`, the scope-gate stop) passes CI and silently stops or misreads the extension's chains. So does a format change that makes the extension's parse select different blocks than the tool's filters, and so does a snippet edit that brings back a repeated heading and makes a fixed-name button ambiguous.

All four are carried out as the draft lays them out. The drift-gate job gains Node steps: a pinned `actions/setup-node` at Node 22, then an install, the extension's build, and its test suite, all run in `gurita-vscode/`. That suite holds three checks of its own. The first reads the extension's carried fixed lines against the `## Fixed console lines` table of `docs/skill-reference.md`. The second runs `core/tools/open_questions.py list --without-alternatives` and `--without-recommendation` with `python3` over the committed question documents under `tests/fixtures/` and compares the blocks they select with the extension's parse. The third checks that no `###` heading of `snippets/GURITA_USAGE.md` repeats. The existing pytest steps stay as they are. It carries out the draft's design whole. Any plugin commit that moves a fixed line, a filter's meaning, or a heading's uniqueness fails CI in the same commit, and every guard stands beside the code it guards, in the extension's one language and test runner, so the extension's directory holds its whole contract. It is the largest option. A second toolchain enters the repository's one CI job, with a new action SHA to bump by hand and a Node install on every push. The suite also reparses the fixed-line table in TypeScript, beside the Python helpers `tests/test_fixed_console_lines.py` already has, so the table has two readers to keep in step. The option holds only if the TypeScript side gets a test runner at all, which the sibling question on TypeScript test coverage settles.

All four are carried out, each guard in the language that already reads its input. The drift-gate job gains Node steps (a pinned `actions/setup-node` at Node 22, then the install, the build, and the extension's test suite), and that suite holds the parse check against `open_questions.py list --without-alternatives` and `--without-recommendation` over the committed fixtures. The fixed-line check and the heading-uniqueness check are written as pytest tests under `tests/`. The fixed-line test reuses the table reading `tests/test_fixed_console_lines.py` already does, and the heading test reads `snippets/GURITA_USAGE.md`. Both CI pytest runs collect these two tests, at the pinned interpreter and at the 3.9 floor. Every guard is enforced in CI, the same-commit failure the draft asks for, and the two plugin-facing checks reuse the one existing reader of the fixed-line table rather than adding a TypeScript copy of it. Only the check that needs the extension's own parser runs under Node. The extension's guards are spread over two suites and two toolchains: one part lives beside the extension and one in `tests/`, which until now tests only `core/tools/`. CI still gains the Node steps and their pin. The fixed-line test can be written in Python only if the extension carries its lines in a form Python can read, which the sibling question on fixed-line carriage settles.

Two of the four are carried out, as pytest tests under `tests/` that both existing CI runs collect. One checks the extension's carried fixed lines against the `## Fixed console lines` table, reusing the table reading `tests/test_fixed_console_lines.py` already does. The other checks that no `###` heading of `snippets/GURITA_USAGE.md` repeats. The drift-gate workflow gains no Node step: the extension's build and tests run in CI nowhere. The parse check against `open_questions.py list --without-alternatives` and `--without-recommendation` is left out. The Node steps and the parse check are written into the follow-up documents under `ideas/`. It guards the two drifts a plugin change is most likely to cause, a fixed line reworded or a snippet heading duplicated, and makes them fail CI in the same commit. CI keeps its single Python toolchain, gains no new action pin, and needs no step added to the workflow file. The extension's own code goes unchecked in CI: a broken TypeScript build lands without notice, and a change to the question document format that moves what the extension's parse selects is caught only when the maintainer sees a wrong label. `tests/` gains tests of a directory outside `core/`. The fixed-line test can be written in Python only if the extension carries its lines in a form Python can read, which the sibling question on fixed-line carriage settles.

All three cross-checks are written, but only the Python ones are enforced in CI. The fixed-line check and the heading-uniqueness check are pytest tests under `tests/`, collected by both existing CI runs, the fixed-line test reusing the table reading of `tests/test_fixed_console_lines.py`. The parse check against `open_questions.py list --without-alternatives` and `--without-recommendation` over the committed fixtures goes into the extension's own Node test suite, which the maintainer runs by hand through nvm. The drift-gate workflow gains no Node step, and the Node steps in CI are written into the follow-up documents under `ideas/`. Every check the draft names exists, and CI keeps one toolchain. The two drifts the plugin causes most easily fail CI in the same commit, and the parse check is one local test command away whenever the question format or the extension's parser changes. The parse check, and the extension's build and tests with it, hold only when someone remembers to run them. A plugin change to the question format can therefore pass CI and break the extension's labels until the next local run. The extension's guards also sit in two places, split by whether CI runs them. The option holds only if the TypeScript side gets a test runner (the sibling question on TypeScript test coverage) and only if the fixed lines are carried in a form Python can read (the sibling question on fixed-line carriage).

The three cross-checks are written into the extension's own Node test suite: fixed lines against the `## Fixed console lines` table, the parse against `open_questions.py list --without-alternatives` and `--without-recommendation` over the committed fixtures, and the snippet headings for repeats. The maintainer runs that suite by hand through nvm beside the extension's build. `.github/workflows/drift-gate.yml` stays unchanged and `tests/` gains nothing. Wiring the suite into the drift-gate workflow is written into the follow-up documents under `ideas/`. Every guard exists and sits beside the code it guards, in one language and one suite, while the repository's CI and its Python test suite stay exactly as they are. Moving the guards into CI later becomes a matter of adding steps to the workflow rather than writing tests. Nothing is enforced. A plugin commit that moves a fixed line, a filter's meaning, or a heading's uniqueness passes CI, and the drift shows only at the next hand run. That gives up the same-commit failure the draft gives as the reason for keeping the extension in this repository. The fixed-line table also gains a TypeScript reader beside the Python one. The option holds only if the TypeScript side gets a test runner, which the sibling question on TypeScript test coverage settles.
